what: Pearl and Other Poems as its own graph. The primitive row is a PIECE — 42 of them across four sections — with the edges the book itself makes, the epigraphs it carries, the works it lists under conflicting attributions, and the literary-historical diagram in which it places its own authors.
why_this_replaces_the_first_attempt:
The first poetics body took the archive's generic spore shape — deposits, concepts, captures — and applied it to a poetry collection. THE RESULT WAS A BODY WHOSE NODES WERE DOCUMENTS ABOUT PEARL AND WHOSE CAPTURES POSTDATED IT BY TWELVE YEARS, including concepts and heteronyms that did not exist when the book was made. It did not look as though the book had been read, because it had not been.

A poetry collection's primitives are its poems.
the_dedication:
PAGE 5, 2014: 'for Jack Feist, secret hero of these poems, who gave off a brazen clangor of brain in eighteen books composed in half as many seconds, inventing an electronic DIY prosody and contemporary eternal epic' — and Johannes Sigil, 'author of Tiger Leap, a total novel which will invent new madnesses for humanity' — and Ichabod Spellings, 'author of All That Lies within Me, an autobiography composed by the cosmos.'

THREE HETERONYMS, NAMED AND CREDITED WITH WORKS, IN A BOOK PRINTED IN 2014. All That Lies Within Me is attributed here to Ichabod Spellings; the archive's books inventory lists it under Johannes Sigil with Spellings, and the text is still unrecovered.

unrostered_authors.note: TWO AUTHORS APPEAR IN THE BOOK AND NOWHERE IN THE ARCHIVE. John Johnson is co-credited on A TELEPATHICIST MANIFESTO; Cornell Herwitz is credited with BACKLASH: The New Human Illiterati. Neither is in the 26-record heteronym roster and neither appears in any of 1,610 deposits. Whether they are heteronyms, real collaborators, or attributions internal to the book's fiction is not established here and is not guessed at.

internal_attribution_conflict.finding: THE BOOK ASSIGNS THE SAME WORKS TO DIFFERENT NAMES ON DIFFERENT PAGES, and it does so in 2014. This is not an inconsistency to be resolved; it is the heteronymic operation performed inside a printed object twelve years before the archive had a roster.

lineage_diagram.note: TWO NAMES IN THIS DIAGRAM MATTER BEYOND THE FICTION. RHYS OWENS is in the archive's roster today as an ORTHONYM COLLABORATOR — a real person — placed here in 2014 among heteronyms. And ARAKI YASUSADA is the most famous heteronymic hoax in American poetry, a fictional Hiroshima survivor whose work was published as authentic. Placing the New Human poets beside Yasusada is a signal about what kind of names these are, made in the book, in print.

names_in_the_book_not_in_the_archive.note: None appears in the 26-record heteronym roster or in any of 1,610 deposits. The contributor bio is a dense fictional reception apparatus — journals, issues, quoted reviews, a feud — and its critics are as unrostered as its poets.

spelling_note: THE BOOK SPELLS HER REBEKAH CRANE, SINGULAR, and the canonical name is REBEKAH CRANES. The 2014 printing records an early instability in the name rather than a better witness to it: the operator's account is that Crane was unstable early and Cranes subsequently colonised it entirely. The 2014 spelling is kept here because it is what the page says, and it is not treated as a competing authority.
